Class GridElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<GridElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.ContainerElement<GridElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.GridElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class GridElement extends ContainerElement<GridElement>
A CSS Grid-inspired layout container that arranges children into a grid with explicit control over grid dimensions, per-column/per-row sizing constraints, and gutter spacing.

Unlike ColumnsElement (which auto-calculates column count from child widths), GridElement provides explicit control over grid dimensions via gridSize(int, int), per-column constraints via gridColumns(Constraint...), per-row constraints via gridRows(Constraint...), and gutter spacing via gutter(int).

When grid-size is not set, auto-sizing uses ceil(sqrt(n)) columns. Column/row constraints cycle when fewer constraints than grid dimensions (matching Textual behavior).

All layout properties can be set via CSS or programmatically. Programmatic values override CSS values when both are set.

Supported CSS properties:

  • grid-size — "3" (3 columns, auto rows) or "3 4" (3 columns, 4 rows)
  • grid-columns — space-separated constraint list, e.g. "fill fill(2) 20"
  • grid-rows — space-separated constraint list, e.g. "2 3"
  • grid-gutter — "2" (uniform) or "1 2" (horizontal vertical)
  • flex — "start", "center", "end", "space-between", "space-around", "space-evenly"
  • margin — margin around the grid

Example usage: 

grid(text("A"), text("B"), text("C"), text("D")).gridSize(2).gutter(1)

    • gridAreas

      public GridElement gridAreas(String... rowTemplates)
      Defines the grid layout using CSS grid-template-areas style strings.

      Each string represents a row. Area names are space-separated tokens. Use "." for empty cells. Area names must form contiguous rectangles.

      When using area-based layout, use area(String, Element) to assign elements to named areas instead of adding children directly. 

      grid()
    .gridAreas("header header header",
               "nav    main   main",
               "nav    main   main",
               "footer footer footer")
    .area("header", text("Header"))
    .area("nav", menu)
    .area("main", content)
    .area("footer", statusBar)
      Parameters:
      rowTemplates - the row templates
      Returns:
      this grid for method chaining
      Throws:
      LayoutException - if the template is invalid

    • area

      public GridElement area(String areaName, Element element)
      Assigns an element to a named area.

      Must be called after gridAreas(String...). Areas without assigned elements render as empty space.

      Parameters:
      areaName - the area name from the template
      element - the element to place in that area
      Returns:
      this grid for method chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if gridAreas() was not called first
      LayoutException - if the area name is not defined in the template

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
